# action.docker_exec

<!-- Code generated by tools/genskill from the provider schema. DO NOT EDIT. -->

Kind: action. Back to [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md).

Runs a command inside a running container, like `docker exec`, and fails when it exits non-zero. stdout and stderr are streamed line by line as action progress and to the provider log; on failure the error carries the exit code and the last 20 lines of output. The result object (`GET /exec/{id}/json`: `exit_code`, `pid`, `process_config`, ...) and the captured `stdout` / `stderr` (up to 4 MiB each, with their `*_sha256`) go to the final progress message and to `result_path`. Runs through the Engine exec API; no docker CLI is involved.

Actions need Terraform >= 1.14. They keep no state: they run when a
resource's `lifecycle { action_trigger { ... } }` fires, or on demand with
`terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_exec.<name>`. Arguments go inside
the action's `config` block.

## Usage

```terraform
action "docker_exec" "<name>" {
  config {
    # arguments below
  }
}

# Run it: lifecycle { action_trigger { events = [after_create] actions = [action.docker_exec.<name>] } }
# on a resource, or: terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_exec.<name>
```

## Arguments and attributes

| Name | Type | Status | Forces replacement | Sensitive | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `command` | `list(string)` | required |  |  | Command and arguments, exec form, e.g. `["sh", "-c", "echo hello"]`. No shell is added. |
| `console_size` | `list(number)` | optional |  |  | Initial terminal size as `[height, width]` (Engine `ConsoleSize`); only with `tty = true`, e.g. for programs that format output to the terminal width. |
| `container_id` | `string` | optional |  |  | The running container to run the command in, by ID or name, e.g. `docker_container.app.id`. Exactly one of `container_id` and `service_id`. |
| `detach` | `bool` | optional |  |  | Start the command and return at once without waiting for it (`docker exec --detach`). Default `false`. Output is not captured and the exit code is not checked. |
| `env` | `map(string)` | optional |  |  | Extra environment variables for the command. They override `env_file` entries. |
| `env_file` | `list(string)` | optional |  |  | Local files of `KEY=VALUE` lines read on the machine running Terraform, like `docker exec --env-file`; `#` comments and blank lines are skipped and a bare `KEY` takes the value from Terraform's environment. |
| `privileged` | `bool` | optional |  |  | Give the command extended privileges. Default `false`. |
| `result_path` | `string` | optional |  |  | Local file the action writes its result object to after a successful run. The file holds one JSON object keyed by the action's output names (`result`, the identity values, the raw outputs with their `*_sha256` hashes, and the version values), with keys sorted at every level, two-space indentation and a trailing newline; it is written atomically (temporary file, then rename) and parent directories are created. Read it in a later run with `jsondecode(file(...))` or the `local_file` data source. Sensitive values are written in full, since this is your own file, but show as `(sensitive)` in the progress message. Nothing is written when the action fails. |
| `service_id` | `string` | optional |  |  | A Swarm service, by name: the command runs in one running task container of it on the provider's daemon (the first by name). Pin the service to that node with a placement constraint. Exactly one of `container_id` and `service_id`. |
| `stdin` | `string` | optional |  |  | Data written to the command's standard input, which is then closed, like `echo ... \| docker exec -i`. Unset (the default), the command gets no stdin. It is never logged or written to `result_path`, but action arguments cannot be marked sensitive or write-only (terraform-plugin-framework v1.19), so pass secrets through `docker_exec_output`, whose `stdin` is sensitive. Not with `tty` or `detach`. |
| `timeout` | `string` | optional |  |  | How long the command may run, as a Go duration (`30s`, `10m`). Default `5m`. On timeout the action fails; the process keeps running in the container. |
| `tty` | `bool` | optional |  |  | Allocate a pseudo-TTY (`docker exec --tty`). Default `false`. With a TTY, stdout and stderr arrive merged in `stdout`. |
| `user` | `string` | optional |  |  | User (and optional group) to run as, `name\|uid[:group\|gid]`. Default: the container's user. |
| `workdir` | `string` | optional |  |  | Working directory inside the container. Default: the container's working directory. |

## Example

```terraform
resource "docker_container" "db" {
  name  = "db"
  image = "postgres:17"

  lifecycle {
    action_trigger {
      events  = [after_create, after_update]
      actions = [action.docker_exec.migrate]
    }
  }
}

# Runs after the container is created or updated; fails the apply when the
# command exits non-zero. Run it on demand with:
#   terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_exec.migrate
action "docker_exec" "migrate" {
  config {
    container_id = docker_container.db.id
    command      = ["sh", "-c", "until pg_isready -U postgres; do sleep 1; done; psql -U postgres -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1"]
    # The SQL script on standard input (`docker exec -i`); psql reads it to
    # end of file. stdin may show in plan output: read secrets with the
    # docker_exec_output ephemeral resource instead.
    stdin   = <<-EOT
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS t (id int);
      INSERT INTO t VALUES (1);
    EOT
    env     = { PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT = "5" }
    user    = "postgres"
    workdir = "/tmp"
    timeout = "2m"
    # A TTY with a fixed size (height, width) for tools that format to it;
    # stdout and stderr then arrive merged in stdout. Not together with stdin.
    # tty          = true
    # console_size = [40, 160]
    # stdout, stderr and the exec inspect (exit_code, pid, ...) as JSON.
    result_path = "${path.module}/out/migrate.json"
  }
}
```
